lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Orbit Roots, one oh nine point three. From the Greenhouse Ring, where nothing is in a hurry. Least of all me.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: You're listening to Orbit Roots. Sister Meridian, on the porch, by the speaker stack. The tomatoes can hear you too. Be kind.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Orbit Roots, from the moon that feeds three systems. If you ate a salad this week, it heard us first.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Good morning from Orbit Roots. The misters are on, the ring is up, and the beans grew another metre in the night. Give thanks.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Orbit Roots, on the farm moon. The ring is low, and the bass goes down to the roots. Where it belongs.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: The irrigation on this moon runs on the off-beat. It always has. Whoever built these pumps knew exactly what they were doing.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Every second beat, a little water. Every second beat, a little bass. Everything on this moon grows on the off-beat. Including me.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: People ask why our tomatoes are so big. Some of it is the low gravity. Most of it is the speaker stack.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: The tomatoes by the porch are two weeks ahead of the tomatoes by the office. Nobody is surprised. The office plays nothing all day. The office plays spreadsheets.

clips.title: A Letter on Very Nice Paper

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: A letter came up today from Clearline Holdings, three systems away. Very nice paper. It says the water that comes down off the rings belongs to them.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Now. That ice was falling off those rings before there was paper. Before there were letters. It will still be falling after.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: We wrote back. On a cabbage leaf. Here's a tune while it gets there.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Shade is precious on a greenhouse moon. So when a little shadow called Greg turned up and stood over the lettuce bed all afternoon, the lettuce was very grateful.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: He says he's on his way home, to a man called Hollis. He's welcome back any time. The spinach is jealous.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Bev called again. She was looking for the request line. She got the pump house.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Brother Amos took her request anyway. He can't play records down there, so he played it on the pipes. She says it wasn't her song. But the carrots haven't stopped talking about it.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: A word for the operator on the relay ship, passing over us in the night. We saw your running lights go across the ring.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: You've drifted a long way out to find us, out here on the edge of the dial. You're welcome. Wipe your feet. There's soil on everything.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: This hour comes to you with the help of Grumbel's Ladders. In low gravity the runner beans grow straight up into the dark, and somebody has to go up after them.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. Some days, up is a bean.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Mother Hale has farmed this moon for sixty years. She says the secret is patience, good soil, and never arguing with a pumpkin that has decided to float.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: This one's for Mother Hale. Turn it up a little. She's in the far greenhouse, and she says the young ones play everything too quiet.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Afternoon on the farm moon. Oldwater is high, the misters are turning in slow circles, and somewhere in greenhouse nine, a bee is flying sideways.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Low gravity. She's doing her best. So are we all.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Bring a seed, take a seed. The Ringside Seed Exchange, behind the packing shed. Open whenever somebody is there, which is usually Mother Hale.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: No money changes hands. Money doesn't grow here. We tried. We planted some. Nothing came up but a letter from the bank.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: The Ringside Seed Exchange. Everything you plant comes back. Mostly.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: A notice from the Greenhouse Ring Co-operative. When the pumps are running, please don't stand on the pipes.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: When the pumps are not running, please also don't stand on the pipes. They're old. They've carried a great deal of water for a great many people. They've done enough.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Respect the pipes.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Time for the crop report, from greenhouse one, all the way round to greenhouse forty.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Crop report. Brother Amos, how's the ring looking?

lines.speaker: Brother Amos, the Pump House
lines.text: Green, Sister. Mostly green.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Runner beans. Up another metre. The tallest has gone through the roof panel in greenhouse twelve and is now, technically, in space. We've sent somebody up with a ladder and a very long piece of string.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Cabbages. Heavy. On a moon like this, heavy is the highest compliment there is. The cabbage crew are walking taller today.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Pumpkins. Three of them have floated off the patch and are drifting slowly towards the packing shed. Leave them. They know the way. They do this every season.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Water. The ice came down off the rings this morning, clean and cold, the same as it has every morning for a thousand years. Nobody sent us a bill. Not yet. Give thanks anyway.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: That's the crop report. Eat your greens. Somebody up here grew them for you.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Good morning. This is First Light Irrigation, on Orbit Roots. The misters are coming on, all the way round the ring. Wake up gently. The lettuce is.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Morning word from the pump house. Brother Amos?

lines.speaker: Brother Amos, the Pump House
lines.text: Pressure's good, Sister. Pipes are singing. And one sprinkler in row six has turned round to face the speaker stack again.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Leave it be. It knows what it likes. This one's for row six.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: This is the Long Table, on Orbit Roots. Pull up a crate. Lunch is whatever's ripe. Today, that's nearly everything.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: At the long table today, the children of the co-op took on the big question. Who owns the water?

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: They said the water belongs to the ice. The ice belongs to the rings. And the rings belong to nobody, because nobody can reach them.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: I've been trying to say that for thirty years. They did it before pudding.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Mother Hale has the floor. She says if a company in another system owns our water, then the company is welcome to come up here and drink it.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: She's laid them a place at the long table. It's been empty for eleven years. She still puts a spoon out.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Deep Roots, on Orbit Roots. The greenhouses are dark, the plants are sleeping, and the bass is going down into the soil. The roots are awake. They always are.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: This is the hour the roots listen hardest. Down in the soil the bass travels further than the light ever gets.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Somewhere under greenhouse four, a carrot is having the best night of its life. Let's not stop now.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: It's nearly Halloween, and the pumpkins have heard. Every one of them has floated up to the glass, facing out, very still.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: We don't carve them here. We ask. Two have said yes. One is thinking about it. Here's a tune for the one that's thinking.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: A moon has gone missing, they say. We checked. We're still here. Feet on the soil.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: But if it was yours, and it's lost, the light's on in the greenhouse. Moons are welcome. Bring your own water.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: The whole ring smells of toast. We don't make toast up here. We grow the wheat, and somebody else does the rest.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: So somebody, somewhere, has finished the job. Give thanks.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: The harvest crew are all humming the same tune, and none of them can finish it. The sprinklers are humming it too.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Bev has rung the pump house to say it's her song. She's probably right.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Three knocks on the shack door, just now. Nobody there. Only the misters, and the ring.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: If that was Clearline Holdings, we're out. In the fields. All of us. For years.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: The sky above the greenhouses has gone a colour I don't have a word for. Every lettuce on the moon has turned to face it.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: They know something. They're not saying.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: A pigeon has walked into the shack. On a farm moon. It went straight to the seed trays, then looked at me like I owed it something.

lines.speaker: Sister Meridian
lines.text: Maybe I do. Help yourself, friend.
